item.title: Building an Agentic Pipeline for Onchain Data Analysis
item.description:
Using an LLM for data analysis can sometimes create more problems than it solves. In a chat-based workflow, the analyst still has to supply table schemas, API documentation, and project-specific context while copying and pasting data between multiple interfaces and tools. If you’re not careful, this setup can increase token costs and introduce errors – undermining the time saved by using an LLM in the first place.

At Blocmates, we created an agentic pipeline to automate these tasks. Instead of manually providing context and coordinating each step, the analyst fills out a data specification and sends it to Claude Code. The agent loads the necessary context, writes SQL queries, fetches data from APIs, and tests and publishes the queries to Dune.

item.title: Building a Local AI System for Financial Markets & Digital Asset Intelligence
item.description:
Financial markets generate an enormous amount of information every day, from macroeconomic developments to digital asset markets and protocol governance. Keeping up with these developments while writing research reports can be time-consuming.

To streamline my research process, I built a locally hosted AI system that aggregates news and market data, identifies important developments, and generates daily research briefings. Using locally hosted language models, the system has reduced my daily news intake from 1–2 hours to approximately 20 minutes.
